Mockup 37, v15. vos-ship-concepts. A militia of traders: six specialists built from freighter hulls only, with their rooms, and three fighters, every one of them detailed and textured.

Notes

Version 15 (you: "I don't really like these glowy bits on the cross. They look kinda cheap to me. If you're gonna have glowy bits use baked lighting or shaders"). No glow is painted any more. The gun mouths, the tractor emitters and the drives are dark lenses in the textures, the light they throw on the hull round them stays baked in, and each glows by a shader: a hot core fading to a dark lip, a rim that lights as you look across it, slow rings drawn inward, each pulsing on its own time.

Version 11 (you: "No two antenna cam be the same shape. Also need dishes as well. Containers need materials. We can reuse that from freighters. And we should begin texture work on all other ships"). Every ship is now detailed and textured: the Boarder, the Drum, the Cross, the Ram and the Broadside on the Deck runner's recipe (their freighter parts in their trade houses' looks gone dull, the militia's welds in rust, windows from their rooms, machinery on every bare face, inset machinery panels, a brass band where the trade was welded on), and the 23 Stack as a fighter. Every antenna and dish on a ship is a design of its own (its head, arms, segments, dish and lean) and a length of its own, at least 12% from every other (you: "No two antenna shall have same length"), a port and starboard pair included (you: "I literally just told you no two antenna should look the same on a starship"), and ships carry dishes on pedestals. The containers now wear the freighters' container, ribs, frames and all, in two tints.

Version 10 (you: "I exepect greebles and antena here", "there should be noface that is completely devoid of detail", with reference ships for the bow and for "the homeworld greeble pattern on hull plating"). No face is plain now. The Deck runner's bow face is filled by a framed panel of machinery laid out in a grid; inset machinery panels run in pairs along its bow end and its drive block; every bare end face carries machinery; and its antennas stand off the hull as real, chunky masts (a block footing, stepped sections, an equipment head, a lit spike, a cross arm with aerials, a dish over flight control). Pick 8 and orbit round to the bow.

Version 9 (you: "other than freighter hulls lets not reuse any other ships hulls too", "I dont like that they have military ship parts, the vos would be sort of a militia organzide from various traders"). No Vos ship carries a warship's part now. Every hull is the game's freighters, cut and joined, and what the militia adds is welded in its own yards. The Saucer runner lost the Concord Petrel and is now the Deck runner: two Hunt freighters joined, one's drive block and the other's bow end, cut short and capped flat. The Boarder's Hunt frigate prow is now a welded lock house with a grapple fork of two blunt arms. The Ram's Albatross nacelles are now two welded drive pods.

The Deck runner is detailed with its rooms: a window wherever its people live or work against the hull. Both freighter parts wear the Hunt freighters' olive gone dull, and the militia's collar and flight deck are rust plate with brass bands. Its seams are now fine and square (you: "lihnes are too harsh, and hull plating lines are crossing over each other"): narrow welds in a colour a little darker than the plate, every cut square to the ship so seams meet and never cross. Lamps run down both edges of the flight deck; its containers are still the plain placed cargo the freighters carry.

Version 8 (you: "ok go ahead, room plan should be included in that detailing"). Every specialist has its rooms planned: pick one and press Rooms to see them inside a see-through hull, with its deck plans below. A Vos ship is a freighter with parts welded on, so its rooms are fitted into hulls that already exist, measured part by part: bridge, bunks, mess, engineering and the hold for taken goods in the drive block, and each trade's own rooms where its parts are (the Deck runner's flight control in its second freighter's bow end, the Ram's blast shelter behind its hammer head, the Broadside's gun crews beside their gun houses).

Version 7 (you: "love all 3 of those fighters, lets stick to 21 as standard fighter, twin boom as the shuttle stand in ( but also they will be used as bombers as well) and lets get highres versions fo these built out"). The Cutter and the Twin boom are detailed: each unwrapped on its own and plated in the Breakers' way, a patchwork of salvaged plate welded plain (rusts, with a plate here and there still in another navy's dulled colour), two thin brass bands, a strapped canopy, and verdigris light in the drive and the gun mouths. Pick 21 or 22, then Painted or PBR, and Night for their hull lights. Blockout and Clay show the welded shape underneath.

Version 6 (you: "pirate fighters need to be unique, like more fighter looking!"). Three fighters of the Syndicate's own, 21 Cutter, 22 Twin boom and 23 Stack, each about 16 m: wings, guns out at the tips or under the nose, one or two big engines and a blunt glazed nose. A fighter is small enough for a clan's yard to weld whole round a salvaged engine, so these are the one thing the Vos build. The Saucer runner now carries six Cutters in place of the stolen Institute fighters. They are tiny on the board; pick one in the list to see it close.

Version 5 (you: "the ships I wanted were not 5,6 it was saucer runner and boarder"; "they are all roughly cruiser sized ships with hull on the lower side, but all are specialized"; "and of course, disguising themselves as freighters too"). The Boarder and the Saucer runner are back; the Twin haul, the Prize frigate, the Castle and the Delta are off the board.

The Vos have no ladder of bigger and bigger classes. Every ship is about cruiser size, 150 to 180 m, built on a freighter's drive block and a short length of its spine, with a weaker hull than a warship of its size. Each has one trade: the Boarder boards, the Drum lays mines, the Cross holds with tractor beams, the Ram breaks rocks, the Deck runner launches fighters, and the Broadside is the one that passes closest as a freighter.

All six are made of freighter parts, so all of them read as freighters from far off. That is the disguise.

Version 4 (you: "I also dont like pointy noses, please fix that"). Every bow the Syndicate welds now ends in a flat face: a blunt armoured bulkhead, a glazed face, or the Ram's hammer head.

Version 3 (you: "6 and 5 are cool, but I would like you to create some unique battle freighter designs"). Six battle freighters whose layouts are the Syndicate's own replace version 2's other conversions.

Each is still made the way a clan makes a ship: a real freighter's drive block and spine, cut to length, with the game's containers bolted on. What is new is the arrangement, and each arrangement is for fighting: a gun line, a drum of missile pods, a cross of gun arms, an armoured ram, a stern tower, two swept wings.

A container on these ships is never just cargo. It is a gun house, a missile pod, a magazine or quarters for a boarding crew, which is why a battle freighter still looks like a freighter.

Freighter parts are the game's own freighters at true size, in a dulled version of their trade houses' colours. The militia's own metal (armour, arms, hubs, pods, guns) is rust plate with a brass rail; a gun's mouth is lit verdigris.
